title: Self-Funded Health, PBM & Workers' Comp Arbitrage — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: Funding Architecture, Stop-Loss Layers, Medical Captives, and PBM Money Trails: Operator Worksheets for Employers Leaving Guaranteed-Cost Health Plans

worksheets.title: Funding Architecture and Level-Funding Readiness Audit
worksheets.purpose: Decide whether the group should stay fully insured, move to level funding, or graduate to traditional self-funding by quantifying the dollars the carrier keeps, the load inside flat quotes, the surplus terms on offer, and the downside exposure if year two turns ugly.
instructions: Start with the most recent renewal and the last full plan year of premium and paid claims before looking at any new quote.
Fill every field with dollar figures or exact contract wording; a field answered with an adjective is not answered.
Request itemized quotes and surplus language in writing from the carrier or broker before scoring any option.
Run the walk-away screen before investing time in underwriting paperwork, so an unfit group never reaches submission.
Review the completed sheet with the owner, confirm the business horizon and cash reserve, and only then authorize binding.

fields.name: current_renewal_loss_ratio
fields.prompt: Pull your last fully insured renewal and calculate your loss ratio by dividing paid claims by total premium. Record the premium, the claims, the dollars the carrier kept, and whether any credit, refund, or rate relief came back to you.
fields.example: A 120-employee Dallas group paid about $1.4 million in premium at a 60% loss ratio and received a flat renewal with no refund, leaving roughly $560,000 with the carrier [AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained — wshiRRBh4Gs @ 00:03:45]. Log: premium $1.4M, claims about $840,000, retained $560,000, credit $0, renewal flat. Flag as a self-funding candidate.

fields.name: funding_model_map
fields.prompt: Map your current and candidate funding models side by side: fully insured, level-funded, and traditional self-funded. For each, note who keeps unspent claims dollars, what portion is fixed versus variable, and what happens to surplus at year end.
fields.example: Fully insured: carrier keeps every unspent dollar. Self-funded: about 60 to 70% of spend is claims, so that share becomes variable and manageable [Self-Funded — VPeObJ32l7M @ 00:03:36]. Level-funded: one flat monthly bill split into admin, stop-loss, and a claims fund, with 50 to 80% of surplus returned depending on contract [Tyler Dutchover — ExcUj28jzzc @ 00:03:47].

fields.name: carrier_load_check
fields.prompt: Ask the carrier or broker to break the level-funded quote into admin, individual stop-loss, aggregate stop-loss, and claims fund. Estimate how much load sits above expected cost and write down whether the flat number was ever itemized for you.
fields.example: Matt Roy says carriers price admin, ISL, ASL and claims, then usually charge about 25% more than they expect it to cost and present one flat number [Blue Ocean Benefits & Consulting — D23XjGg7o_g @ 00:05:15]. Entry: flat quote received, itemization requested in writing, and every line treated as carrying that 25% load until the carrier shows the expected-claims figure separately.

fields.name: surplus_split_language
fields.prompt: Quote the exact surplus-split and renewal language from the level-funded contract. Record the refund percentage, whether it arrives as cash or as lower rates, the runout period that delays payment, and how long the owner expects to stay in business.
fields.example: Security Health Plan currently refunds 66% of unused claim dollars at the end of the run-out period [Security Health Plan — 8FR_2qIAL34 @ 00:15:46]. ATA advises asking the owner how long they expect to be in business and setting the split to that horizon [American Trust Administrators | Level Funding — 8scqEaAolto @ 00:05:56]. Entry: 66% refund, 12/18 runout, owner horizon ten-plus years.

fields.name: year_two_downside
fields.prompt: Model the year-two downside before binding. Write the worst plausible renewal: a laser on one high-cost employee, the fully insured fallback rate if you return, and the cash the business could write if aggregate claims hit early in the year.
fields.example: Tyler Dutchover flags a renewal laser that pushes one employee's specific attachment to $200,000, plus a 10 percent or higher fully insured fallback rate [Tyler Dutchover — m5BLhBDIZZ4 @ 00:06:25]. On traditional self-funding, prove the business can write a check for the full aggregate within a couple of months [Maximize Asset Protection — hqPZ5l67B4A @ 00:17:42]. Entry: both scenarios priced, cash reserve confirmed.

fields.name: group_fit_screen
fields.prompt: Screen the group against the walk-away conditions. Note claims history versus average, emergency room use, owner plans to sell within one to two years, demographics, expected utilization, and whether the client accepts a full 12-month contract with delayed surplus.
fields.example: ATA says walk away if the group runs above-average claims, shows high ER use, or the owner plans to sell within one to two years [American Trust Administrators | Level Funding — dgpkKOJBv_s @ 00:01:22]. JS Benefits Group warns against picking level funding just because the first quote looks cheaper [JS Benefits Group — qE34fv4L2qU @ 00:00:54]. Entry: claims average, no sale planned.

fields.name: underwriting_packet
fields.prompt: List every underwriting document the quote requires and its status: individual health questionnaires, census with SIC code and zip, quarterly wage and tax filing, and enrollment forms. Record the owner's hard deadline and who is chasing missing employees.
fields.example: ATA budgets 5 to 10 minutes per employee for IHQs [American Trust Administrators | Level Funding — ise8qdroICE @ 00:02:28], and Warp notes some carriers require an IMQ taking three to five minutes each [Warp — XHSDGFk6y94 @ 00:02:08]. Entry: owner sets a Friday deadline [American Trust Administrators | Level Funding — E2z3UzEl2Ds @ 00:01:14]; census, wage report and all IHQs held until complete.

fields.name: broker_compensation_model
fields.prompt: Write how your broker is paid today and how that pay would change under a fee model. Note whether the broker will grind level-funding paperwork, whether they quoted alternatives at all, and whether you need a different broker.
fields.example: Self Insured Reporting recommends converting 5% commission into a visible fee paid like an accountant or attorney [Self Insured Reporting — 5PxkF9WUCd0 @ 00:05:13]. Warp says typical brokers skip level funding because of extra work [Warp — XHSDGFk6y94 @ 00:00:48], and ATA adds: 'If your broker refuses to look, find another broker' [American Trust Administrators | Level Funding — ise8qdroICE @ 00:05:50].

fields.name: plan_redesign_levers
fields.prompt: Inventory the plan redesign levers available inside a level-funded or self-funded structure. Note network options, reference-based access fees, direct primary care diversion, site-of-care price gaps, and which admin and stop-loss fees you will reopen at each renewal.
fields.example: Hint Health shows diverted claims worth about $40 PMPM and avoided services about 25 [Hint Health — 5ztwBEIpJjs @ 00:19:47]. BenefitsAlly cites an MRI at $3,200 versus $680 three miles away [BenefitsAlly | Home of the 3x3x3 Challenge — xXX6dBL4p3A @ 00:00:15]. BeneSmart notes admin and stop-loss fees are negotiable annually [BeneSmart - A Modern Approach to Benefits — UOjbo9Dprhw @ 00:05:47].

fields.name: go_live_timeline
fields.prompt: Set the go-live timeline backward from the effective date. Record the enrollment start date, the provider briefing on the new ID card, the expected speed of the level-funded quote, and the data you will harvest for a future self-funding move.
fields.example: BeneSmart starts enrollment 30 days out and briefs providers on the new ID card [BeneSmart - A Modern Approach to Benefits — UOjbo9Dprhw @ 00:09:35]. ATA warns level funding is slower than fully insured [American Trust Administrators | Level Funding — E2z3UzEl2Ds @ 00:03:20]. Allstate considers self-funding under 100 lives with level-funded claims data proving good results [Maximize Asset Protection — hqPZ5l67B4A @ 00:09:05].

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when the loss ratio and retained dollars are calculated, the surplus split and runout are quoted in writing, the year-two laser and fallback scenarios are priced, every IHQ and wage report is collected, and the owner has accepted the 12-month commitment.

worksheets.title: Stop-Loss Contract and Captive Layer Audit
worksheets.purpose: Expose the gaps between a self-funded plan and its stop-loss protection, including lasers, unfiled claims, split medical and pharmacy feeds, and unmirrored plan language, then test whether a member-owned captive offers a more stable layer design for the group.
instructions: Gather the current stop-loss contract, the renewal proposal, the plan document, and all amendments before starting.
Price every laser and corridor in dollars of added exposure, not in percentages alone.
Confirm claim-filing ownership and data feeds with written acknowledgment from the TPA, PBM, and stop-loss carrier.
Begin the captive evaluation four to six months before renewal so actuarial layer work can finish on time.
Escalate any field left blank or contested to the broker and counsel before the renewal is signed.

fields.name: spec_ag_structure
fields.prompt: Record the specific deductible, the aggregate attachment point, and the aggregate corridor percentage on your stop-loss quote. Note what share of stop-loss premium funds the specific layer and whether the aggregate looks conservatively or aggressively set.
fields.example: Spencer calls 25% the most common corridor, so $1M expected claims becomes a $1.25M attachment [Self-Funded — Dy4S9Ie5mEM @ 00:01:15], and warns carriers sometimes get too aggressive on that calculation to win business [Self-Funded — Dy4S9Ie5mEM @ 00:05:34]. Pete Dorne puts 85 to 90% of premium in the specific layer [ParetoHealth — 4VhWXTCGo74 @ 00:01:52].

fields.name: laser_inventory
fields.prompt: Search the renewal for every laser. For each named claimant, record the laser amount, the standard specific deductible, the extra exposure between them, and the counter-offer you will make, such as an aggregating specific deductible or premium relief.
fields.example: A $600,000 laser over a $150,000 spec meant up to $450,000 of extra exposure [Benefit Whisperer — 6E1eObzSNLc @ 00:01:05]. Spencer offers a $50,000 ag spec in exchange for dropping a $125,000 laser on a $100,000 spec, which carriers often accept when it is that close [Self-Funded — VatFfWseBbI @ 00:07:48]. Entry: one laser found, ag spec counter sent.

fields.name: claim_filer_assignment
fields.prompt: Name the single party responsible for filing stop-loss claims, whether TPA, general agent, or broker team. Record how the carrier receives claims, how fast specific claims are submitted after the deductible is met, and who verifies receipt.
fields.example: Spencer fielded broker calls at Sun Life about a $300,000 claim the carrier had never received, because a BUCA ASO setup with a third-party carrier was not sending claims [Self-Funded — AM2DB13I88c @ 00:02:56]. Stop-loss reimburses after the employer pays, with specific claims submitted once the deductible is met [Self Insured Reporting — HuaDk3XBOrc @ 00:02:34]. Entry: TPA named filer.

fields.name: rx_medical_claim_feed
fields.prompt: If the PBM is unbundled from the medical TPA, document how both medical and pharmacy claims reach the stop-loss carrier. Record each data source, the reporting frequency, and the test you ran to confirm split claims count toward the deductible.
fields.example: Spencer warns that in unbundled PBM arrangements the stop-loss carrier must receive medical and Rx claims from their corresponding sources, or split claims get missed and a breached deductible can stay hidden [Self-Funded — AM2DB13I88c @ 00:06:19]. Entry: TPA sends medical monthly, PBM sends Rx monthly, carrier confirmed both feeds in writing, one combined claimant reconciled against the deductible.

fields.name: plan_mirroring
fields.prompt: Compare the plan document to the stop-loss contract clause by clause. Confirm a plan mirroring provision exists, list any plan document amendments, and note every benefit the plan covers that the stop-loss contract could refuse to reimburse.
fields.example: This STUFF is complicated advises looking for plan mirroring language so whatever the plan document covers is covered by the stop-loss contract, and leaning on plan document amendments for extra protection [This STUFF is complicated — q36fieahkDs @ 00:03:37]. Entry: mirroring clause confirmed, two amendments attached, no coverage gaps flagged, counsel sign-off pending before the renewal is bound.

fields.name: renewal_comparison_baseline
fields.prompt: Compare your self-funded attachment point not to today's fully insured renewal but to the renewal you would face twelve months after a bad claims year. Record both numbers and the gap, and note recent large-claim severity trends.
fields.example: ParetoHealth frames the right comparison as a fully insured renewal delayed 12 months, the 30 to 35% hit after a bad year [ParetoHealth — 4VhWXTCGo74 @ 00:10:01]. One stop-loss carrier partner saw a 45% increase in size and severity of large claims, with former $250,000 claims running $500,000 to $600,000 [ParetoHealth — 4VhWXTCGo74 @ 00:02:21].

fields.name: aggregate_value_test
fields.prompt: Decide whether aggregate coverage is worth buying at the quoted price. Record its premium, how often groups actually collect, the corridor used, and whether an experience refund or a straight premium cut better fits your risk appetite.
fields.example: Self-Funded calls aggregate 'sleep insurance' because it is really inexpensive and highly predictable to a stop-loss underwriter [Self-Funded — 4cndcrJWUGg @ 00:05:27]. Pete Dorne reports aggregate claims hit less than 3% of self-funded groups [ParetoHealth — 4VhWXTCGo74 @ 00:08:54]. Tyler Dutchover notes the attachment is usually 125% of expected claims [Tyler Dutchover — b2StkpG4yOY @ 00:03:37].

fields.name: captive_layer_design
fields.prompt: Sketch the captive layer stack you are evaluating: the specific deductible you retain, the member-owned pool layer above it, the excess carrier on top, the aggregate attachment, and the share of premium ceded to the member loss fund.
fields.example: Captive Resources illustrates Omega choosing a $100,000 specific deductible, meaning the company pays the first $100,000 of any claim [Captive Resources — c_F-WNrCoqk @ 00:03:16]. CRI reports 60 to 65% of premium ceded to the loss fund and $35M returned over 10 years [Christopher Martens — M8zhsS8szwY @ 00:55:23]. Entry: $100,000 retention, pool layer, A-rated excess above.

fields.name: captive_fit_and_timing
fields.prompt: Test captive fit and timing. Record whether leadership treats stop-loss as a commodity, the months remaining before renewal, the captive's common anniversary, whether claims are accruing toward the deductible now, and the first-contract length needed to align.
fields.example: Captives use a common anniversary with short or long first contracts, and you do not move mid-year if claims are accruing to the deductible [Christopher Martens — M8zhsS8szwY @ 01:06:08]. TheSpringGroup starts building 4 to 6 months before renewal [TheSpringGroup — L4bWq8jE_JE @ 00:01:45]. A commodity buyer is not a fit [Self-Funded — 8nD9sJwgMdE @ 00:05:41].

fields.name: captive_downside_and_reserves
fields.prompt: Run the downside and upside of captive membership. Record the look-back of historical large claims against the member bucket, the chance of an assessment year, the program's retention rate, and how you would deploy accumulated reserves.
fields.example: Captive Resources runs a look-back analysis of large claims against the member bucket [Captive Resources — BQVeLgnIx8A @ 00:15:20] and reports 98 plus percent retention [Captive Resources — BQVeLgnIx8A @ 00:18:27]. Self-Funded lists three reserve uses: lower deductibles, raise contributions, or grant premium holidays [Self-Funded — 8nD9sJwgMdE @ 00:06:20]. Entry: no assessment signal, reserves earmarked for a premium holiday.

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when every laser is priced and countered, a single claim filer is named, medical and Rx claims are confirmed flowing to the carrier, plan mirroring is verified, and the captive decision is documented against timing, fit, and look-back results.

worksheets.title: PBM Money Trail and Contract Forensics Worksheet
worksheets.purpose: Follow every pharmacy dollar from plan sponsor to PBM, pharmacy, manufacturer, and aggregator, quantify spread and retained rebates at the claim level, and rewrite contract definitions, pricing basis, term, and audit rights so savings flow to the plan instead of the middleman.
instructions: Request claim-level data that shows plan-billed amounts, pharmacy-paid amounts, and pricing basis for at least one generic and one specialty drug.
Read the definitions section of the PBM contract before reading any price guarantee or discount promise.
Put every transparency question and disclosure request in writing and log the date and quality of each response.
Use counsel and advisers with no payment relationship to the PBM when redlining terms.
Carry unresolved findings into the audit plan and the next RFP so they become contract requirements, not open questions.

fields.name: pbm_ownership_map
fields.prompt: Map who owns your PBM and every pharmacy, mail-order, and specialty operation tied to it. Record whether your funding model locks you to the carrier's PBM and whether a carve-out to an independent PBM is available.
fields.example: Dr. Eric Bricker notes that on fully insured plans Cigna requires Express Scripts, Aetna requires CVS Caremark, and United requires OptumRx [AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained — wshiRRBh4Gs @ 00:01:32], while self-funded sponsors can carve out the PBM [AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained — -xH2R8NZ4pU @ 00:12:22]. SmithRx says it owns no pharmacies or supply-chain assets [SmithRx — KB9tHMlyhyA @ 00:00:55].

fields.name: rebate_flow
fields.prompt: Trace rebate dollars from manufacturer to plan. Record the rebate share passed through, the share the PBM retains, whether a rebate aggregator or PBM-owned GPO sits in between, and the administrative fees that never appear in rebate reporting.
fields.example: Bricker estimates 55 to 80 percent of the rebate reaches the plan while the PBM keeps the rest [AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained — vT0NNXYjQ_Y @ 00:03:31]. Frier Levitt says the aggregator keeps about 30 percent and passes 60 to 70 cents to the PBM [Frier Levitt — 8mubYuuHvMI @ 00:01:20]. Entry: aggregator confirmed, GPO fees undisclosed.

fields.name: spread_per_claim
fields.prompt: Pull a sample of generic and specialty claims and place the plan-billed amount next to the pharmacy-paid amount and acquisition cost for each. Record the spread per claim and the multiple of acquisition cost your plan actually paid.
fields.example: Bricker's amlodipine walk-through shows 48 cents billed against 1.9 cents acquisition, almost exactly 25 times more [AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained — 0XFk1m3yGuY @ 00:03:09]. RxPreferred shows a PBM paying the pharmacy $10, invoicing $100 plus a $2 admin fee, and keeping $92 [RxPreferred — 15IQO_jTMUM @ 00:01:17]. Entry: twenty claims sampled, median generic multiple logged.

fields.name: specialty_script_extraction
fields.prompt: Break down one high-cost specialty script end to end. Record what the plan was billed, what the pharmacy was paid, the rebate amount and share retained, any transaction fee, and the total gross dollars the PBM extracted from that fill.
fields.example: Vault of Profit walks a $1,000 specialty script: the PBM bills the employer $940, pays the pharmacy $850, keeps 20 percent of a $400 rebate, and adds a $5 fee, for $175 gross [Vault of Profit — 351RCg-LQ6I @ 00:07:49]. PBM Insider cites an almost 500% average markup on high-cost drugs in the Johnson & Johnson case [PBM Insider — o57C9bK5ouI @ 00:01:20].

fields.name: rebate_definition_clause
fields.prompt: Copy the contract's exact definition of rebate and every related term. Record whether it captures all discounts and amounts based on a percentage of drug cost, or whether narrowed wording leaves bonus payments, market share fees, and GPO fees outside pass-through.
fields.example: Desai warns the rebate definition has been narrowed over the years to create other revenue pockets that escape pass-through [American Health Law Association — bO0c-bD-CEA @ 00:14:31]. Nephron data shows rebates fell from 48% to 13% of PBM profit, so full rebate pass-through leaves 87% untouched [AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained — yFJFnewKqw4 @ 00:08:25]. Entry: definition redlined by counsel.

fields.name: transparency_questions
fields.prompt: Write the transparency questions you will put to the PBM in writing. Include whether it has another customer besides the health plan, disclosure of formulary, market share and bonus payments, and whether any clause calls real drug costs trade secrets.
fields.example: Bricker's key question: does the PBM have another customer besides the health plan, with market share and bonus payments disclosed, not just rebates [AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained — vT0NNXYjQ_Y @ 00:04:07]. Tyler Dutchover says if the PBM can refuse to show the receipts, assume you are paying more than needed [Tyler Dutchover — ufeHEzWD1Cc @ 00:09:52]. Entry: trade-secret clause struck.

fields.name: pass_through_charge_basis
fields.prompt: Test whether a pass-through label is real. Record the basis the plan is charged on, the basis the pharmacy is reimbursed on, whether MAC overperformance flows to you, and whether pricing moves toward NADAC or acquisition cost.
fields.example: Cora Opsahl reports AWP-discount billing to the plan against acquisition-cost-plus reimbursement to the pharmacy [Relentless Health Value — xHAyQelFkf8 @ 00:12:47]. TheCoyPharmer recommends monthly or weekly reporting and NADAC or pass-through pricing so MAC overperformance flows to the sponsor [TheCoyPharmer — H3p5Yw0Y-ek @ 00:15:25]. Entry: charge basis mismatched, NADAC pricing requested in redline.

fields.name: contract_term_and_repricing
fields.prompt: Record the contract length, the annual repricing or market-check provision, the exit penalty, and who reviewed the definitions section. Note whether any adviser on the deal receives payment from the PBM and how that conflict was handled.
fields.example: The Partners Group describes a client trapped in a multi-year deal by stale discounts and an exit penalty above $500K [The Partners Group — Cxvmh46o824 @ 00:44:25]. Frier Levitt urges negotiating down to the definitions section with competent counsel and avoiding consultants paid by the PBM [Frier Levitt — 8mubYuuHvMI @ 00:03:34]. Entry: three-year term, annual repricing added, independent counsel.

fields.name: audit_plan
fields.prompt: Plan the PBM audit. Record audit frequency, the line-level items tested, the expected recovery range, and who will run the audit even when the dollar amount looks too small to chase. Note which overcharge categories you suspect first and why.
fields.example: A jumbo plan sponsor reports audits finding 30 to 40% overcharges, with every audit yielding money back, and notes The Partners Group puts typical findings at 10 to 30% [Relentless Health Value — xHAyQelFkf8 @ 00:16:37]. Frier Levitt hears pharmacies call $5,000 or $10,000 findings too small to challenge [Frier Levitt — 67He43cmPRc @ 00:45:23]. Entry: annual audit, spread and rebates tested.

fields.name: formulary_and_specialty_strategy
fields.prompt: Set the formulary and specialty strategy. List heavily advertised, low-efficacy drugs to replace, the first biosimilar switch for a specialty carve-out, member outreach steps, step-therapy rules, and whether the network RFP will require Cost Plus Drugs participation.
fields.example: Purdue moved Remicade to Inflectra for about 32% year-over-year savings, met with nearly every affected member, and now adds drugs quarterly [Employers' Forum of Indiana — zoRFywXBoLM @ 00:17:56]. Cuban says requiring Cost Plus Drugs in the RFP prompts big PBMs to offer bigger rebates and better terms [Relentless Health Value — xHAyQelFkf8 @ 00:18:34]. Entry: one biosimilar switch scheduled.

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when sample claims show billed versus paid amounts, rebate definitions are redlined to include all discounts, the charge basis matches pharmacy reimbursement, annual repricing and audit rights are written into the contract, and a specialty or formulary action is scheduled.

worksheets.title: Reference-Based Pricing, Direct Contracting & Broker Compensation Audit
worksheets.purpose: Build a defensible reference-based pricing launch plan, map direct-contracting leverage, and expose exactly how your broker is paid before renewing, switching, or issuing a broker of record letter.
instructions: Pull twelve months of claims at the per-employee-per-month level before modeling any reference-based pricing savings, and use matured claims rather than early estimates.

Secure written access to HR and rank-and-file employees for education sessions before go-live, because RBP deals launched without that access went sideways [Dysrupt Healthcare Podcast — mPaz9R2yMrs @ 00:08:26].
Net every TPA, repricing, and advocacy fee against projected savings so the headline percentage reflects true plan spend.
Request the broker's written compensation disclosure in named dollar figures before discussing any renewal, plan redesign, or marketing exercise.
Treat any broker of record letter as a firing decision, not a quoting tool, and complete the remaining fields before signing one.

fields.name: current_pepm_baseline
fields.prompt: Record your plan's current cost per covered employee per month, the network discount structure you pay through, and the percentage savings you would need from a reference-based pricing build to justify switching away from a chargemaster-discount PPO model.
fields.example: A 300-employee blue-collar California agricultural group started at $819 per covered employee per month and landed at $480 after year one, a 41.4% reduction worth about $1.6M, with zero known balance bills across 2,000-plus claims and a stop-loss renewal at minus 10.1% [Dysrupt Healthcare Podcast — mPaz9R2yMrs @ 00:45:10]. Set your own target against that benchmark.

fields.name: facility_payment_formula
fields.prompt: Write the exact facility payment formula your plan will use, including the Medicare multiple, any cost-plus alternative, and which method controls when the two produce different numbers, then note how inpatient bills will be clinically audited line by line.
fields.example: Pay facilities the greater of Medicare plus 25% or the hospital's own self-reported cost plus 20%, run line by line against the cost-of-services report every Medicare-participating hospital files with CMS [Dysrupt Healthcare Podcast — mPaz9R2yMrs @ 00:24:54]. Compare that against the common 150% to 200% of Medicare range [Holloway Benefit Concepts — 2dsXkvZasDU @ 00:00:24].

fields.name: physician_outreach_plan
fields.prompt: List the physicians your members already see, who will call each office before the effective date, and what the outreach script covers about payment terms, payer ID, and the new ID card, so acceptance is secured before claims arrive.
fields.example: Collect member-nominated doctors during enrollment, then call each office before go-live to explain payment terms, payer ID, and the ID card; this outreach produced 95% physician acceptance [Dysrupt Healthcare Podcast — mPaz9R2yMrs @ 00:12:17]. For holdouts, cut single-case agreements, and confirm members check in advance whether a provider accepts RBP pricing [Rhett Robbins — 8begy-typh4 @ 00:01:24].

fields.name: balance_bill_defense
fields.prompt: Describe the balance-bill advocacy structure you will stand up before go-live, who answers the member's first call when a provider demands cash upfront, and whether your posture is pay-and-defend or negotiate-and-settle when a facility disputes the payment.
fields.example: One producer watched a client revert to a conventional PPO within months because employees faced cash-upfront demands and complaints mounted before advocates were in place [Partners MGU — YEFRBSmT3IE @ 00:00:29]. Assign a third-party advocate to step in on billing disputes [Rhett Robbins — 8begy-typh4 @ 00:01:24], and avoid the 1.0 bait-and-switch models that turned litigious [Dysrupt Healthcare Podcast — xVuFXA-gN8g @ 00:07:13].

fields.name: dominant_market_map
fields.prompt: Map every market where a single dominant health system or rural hospital controls access, name the freestanding ambulatory surgery centers you will contract as plan B, and state how members will be steered there before they need surgery.
fields.example: Flag dominant-system and rural markets early and contract freestanding ambulatory surgery centers as the backup before members need procedures [Self-Funded — A__ZFq9k8Ds @ 00:38:56]. Price gaps justify the effort: at one hospital an MRI costs $3,200, while three miles away it runs $680, one-fifth of the price [BenefitsAlly | Home of the 3x3x3 Challenge — xXX6dBL4p3A @ 00:00:15].

fields.name: direct_contract_leverage
fields.prompt: Identify the providers you could contract with directly, the concentrated headcount you can steer to them, how fast your plan can pay compared with major carriers, and what negotiation leverage beyond pure cost analysis you are prepared to use.
fields.example: Offer steerage and faster payment, since major carriers can take 30, 60, even 90 days to pay [AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained — xcu6bvj22fc @ 00:02:17]. Montana cut hospital pay from 191-611% to 200-220% of Medicare, saving $15M on hospitals, only after threatening to publish rates and board contacts and offering free out-of-state transport [AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained — gpm3vtKEf5U @ 00:03:19].

fields.name: dual_option_design
fields.prompt: Sketch a dual-option enrollment design that places the reference-based plan beside a conventional network plan, listing deductible, employee monthly contribution for each, and the enrollment split you expect, plus TPA and repricing fees netted against projected savings.
fields.example: ClaimDOC's first case ran a dual option on the UMR and United network: a $2,000 deductible at $130 a month versus $200 a month for United, and 350 enrolled with ClaimDOC while six picked United [Self-Funded — A__ZFq9k8Ds @ 00:55:41]. Get TPA and repricing fees quoted, because they can eat into the saving [Benefits Studio — noY8cLblMi4 @ 00:01:12].

fields.name: broker_comp_disclosure
fields.prompt: Record every dollar your broker receives, separating base commission, persistency or retention bonuses, and indirect agency-level pay, then note the date you requested the written compensation statement and how quickly and completely the broker actually responded.
fields.example: Request the 408(b)(2) compensation statement in named dollar figures; a confident broker sends it the same week, while stalling or a summary tells you something [Benefits Blake — m68BBrL5G18 @ 00:19:46]. Watch for the line item that pays an advisor for you not to change carriers [Benefits Blake — m68BBrL5G18 @ 00:06:46].

fields.name: peer_benchmark_5500
fields.prompt: Name three peer employers of similar size in your area whose Form 5500 Schedule A filings you pulled, and record what each pays its broker per enrolled person per year compared with your own plan's broker cost.
fields.example: Pull peer Schedule A filings free on EFAST2 [Benefits Blake — m68BBrL5G18 @ 00:16:12], then compare against the $178 median per enrolled person per year, roughly $15 a month, from almost 30,000 fully insured plans [Benefits Blake — m68BBrL5G18 @ 00:02:31]. Treat Schedule A as the floor of compensation, not the ceiling [Benefits Blake — m68BBrL5G18 @ 00:17:00].

fields.name: bor_decision
fields.prompt: State whether you will issue a broker of record letter, the specific reason, such as firing the incumbent or changing market access, whether the carrier accepts midterm changes, and how you will handle the incumbent's rescind request.
fields.example: Sign a BOR only to fire the incumbent or move market access, never because an agent claims it is needed for quotes [Beyond Business Insurance — rnj58CEkGiE @ 00:02:47]. Expect the incumbent to call inside the five-day hold window asking you to rescind, and prepare for the difficult conversation [Strategic Builders-Dev Insurance & Risk Solutions — 79EPdRvCp3A @ 00:01:50].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not launch reference-based pricing or sign a broker of record letter until the facility formula, physician outreach list, balance-bill advocate, plan B surgery centers, netted fee schedule, and written broker compensation disclosure in dollar figures are all documented on this worksheet.

worksheets.title: CAA Compliance, Fiduciary Defense & Claims Administration Control
worksheets.purpose: Document the fiduciary process the CAA now demands of every ERISA health plan sponsor, from gag-clause removal and compensation disclosures to PBM definition audits, vendor liability terms, and claimant-level cost analysis.
instructions: Gather every carrier, ASO, TPA, PBM, broker, and consultant contract currently in force, including amendments, before filling in any field.
Record dates for every request, response, and attestation, because documenting the process matters as much as doing it.
Read contract definitions before price guarantees, and quote exact contract language rather than summarizing it.
Escalate in writing any vendor that refuses gag-clause removal, compensation disclosure, or line-level claims data.
Review this worksheet with fiduciary decision-makers at least annually and before every renewal, RFP, or attestation deadline.

fields.name: fiduciary_roster
fields.prompt: List every person and committee acting as fiduciary for the health plan, which tasks each has delegated to vendors, and which vendors have signed in writing that they accept fiduciary status, noting where liability still rests with the employer.
fields.example: Fully insured employers are now fiduciaries too [Ameriflex — l5tGs_zQ8xA @ 00:04:02]. You can delegate responsibility but never liability [Self-Funded — I7g6idLkgrc @ 00:29:13], and unless vendors sign off as fiduciaries, the liabilities lie with you [OneVision — ks-F1VjDtk4 @ 00:18:05]. Document the process and keep receipts [Walsh Insurance — 9hPiS9wv_F4 @ 00:16:25].

fields.name: gag_clause_inventory
fields.prompt: Inventory every carrier, ASO, TPA, and PBM contract, quote any language restricting access to claims or cost data, record the date each gag clause was removed, and note any vendor refusing removal whose contract cannot be extended.
fields.example: You cannot extend any contract with someone who will not remove the gag clause [Berger Montague — WBl8smrz_3E @ 00:01:38]. The employer carries a new fiduciary duty to vet that those clauses are gone [Mel 😊 DeWeese — k0FZkQKH4SQ @ 00:07:35]. Strike any clause calling real drug costs confidential trade secrets [Tyler Dutchover — ufeHEzWD1Cc @ 00:09:52].

fields.name: attestation_readiness
fields.prompt: Record the date of your annual gag-clause compliance attestation, which internal deadline you are working to, and the claims data pull and audit steps completed beforehand to check for double payments and improper reductions before anyone signs.
fields.example: Plans must attest every single year by December 31st that insurance and pharmacy contracts comply [HUB Midwest East (fka Henriott) — JY_hbh9Kxrc @ 00:01:42], though some practitioners work to December 27. Hold the signature until claims data has actually been pulled and audited for double payments and improper reductions [Berger Montague — WBl8smrz_3E @ 00:03:15].

fields.name: comp_disclosure_tracker
fields.prompt: For each broker or consultant expecting more than $1,000 in direct or indirect compensation, log the disclosure request date, the 30-day response deadline, the dollar figures received, and the 90-day termination date that applies if they never deliver.
fields.example: The trigger is more than $1,000 in expected compensation [The Leapfrog Group — QU7rxyEAEjQ @ 00:10:51]. A Florida school system expected about $195,000 in provider pay over four years and found about $4 million [OneVision — ks-F1VjDtk4 @ 00:17:25]. Do not renew until disclosure arrives; otherwise request it in writing and report to DOL [Berger Montague — 3ZIAPoIvjvc @ 00:03:59].

fields.name: form5500_status
fields.prompt: List every welfare plan requiring a Form 5500, each original due date, whether any filing is late, whether a DOL notice has arrived, and whether an SPD wrap could combine plans under a single DFVCP penalty cap.
fields.example: Late filers face $2,739 per day per plan outside DFVCP versus $10 a day inside, capped at $1,500 small or $4,000 large [HR Service, Inc. — K_Kmaqdjrns @ 00:09:00]. Penalties run from the day after the original due date, not the extension date [HR Service, Inc. — K_Kmaqdjrns @ 00:10:11]. Filing is electronic only.

fields.name: pbm_definitions_audit
fields.prompt: Copy the contract definitions of generic drug, brand drug, specialty drug, and rebate from your PBM agreement, note which pricing basis applies to each category, and flag any definition that lets a generic be relabeled and repriced as specialty.
fields.example: Read definitions before price guarantees [Total Control Health Plans — FvXAV4cqPRg @ 00:03:16]. The J&J plan paid $10,239 for teriflunomide acquired at $81, a 12,403% markup [Total Control Health Plans — FvXAV4cqPRg @ 00:02:29]. Relabeling generics as specialty moves reimbursement from AWP minus 87 percent to AWP minus 12 percent, so lock every definition before renewal.

fields.name: rfp_contract_terms
fields.prompt: List the must-have contract terms you will load into the RFP itself, including limitation of liability, indemnification, data access, lock-in length, and audit rights, and record the liability cap structure each finalist vendor proposed in response.
fields.example: Load must-have terms before vendors respond, because once a vendor knows it won the RFP, employers lose leverage [theallianceorg — 2VQyGj0Z_oY @ 00:40:26]. Typical caps run $50K per error, $1M per claim, or 4x the last 12 months of fees [theallianceorg — 2VQyGj0Z_oY @ 00:38:42]. Contractual indemnification is how to shift TPA-caused costs [Miller Johnson — WVU2CeENchc @ 00:34:53].

fields.name: line_level_pbm_audit
fields.prompt: Describe how you will audit pharmacy claims at the line level, comparing the amount charged to the plan with the amount paid to the pharmacy, and how retained rebates and spread will be quantified rather than relying on discount guarantees.
fields.example: Audit spread line by line, such as $1 charged to the plan versus $0.80 paid to the pharmacy [Frier Levitt — jpLEKhmPpLs @ 00:58:47]. Stop negotiating on discount guarantees, which the same panel calls the wrong questions to be asking [Frier Levitt — jpLEKhmPpLs @ 00:54:25]. A jumbo sponsor reports audits finding 30 to 40% overcharges [Relentless Health Value — xHAyQelFkf8 @ 00:16:37].

fields.name: claimant_concentration
fields.prompt: Using your TPA claims report, count members above $20,000 and above $100,000 in annual cost, classify each large claim as ongoing or complete by diagnosis and procedure code, and name the intervention you will apply to the middle band.
fields.example: Members above $100K form the 5% driving 50% of costs, and members above $20K form the 20% driving 80%, so the sweet spot sits at $20K-$100K [AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained — UQkzQUPP8JE @ 00:02:00]. Cancer and surgical complications keep running, while ortho and heart-attack claims are mostly complete [AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained — UQkzQUPP8JE @ 00:04:10].

fields.name: surcharge_litigation_review
fields.prompt: Review your SPD and every flyer, enrollment guide, and program document describing a tobacco surcharge or wellness program, list each required term and where it appears, and note your documented RFP history in case a fiduciary claim arrives.
fields.example: Audit the SPD and all program materials for any surcharge or wellness program so no required term goes missing from a flyer [The Class Action Weekly Wire — NtoIMU293PI @ 00:07:30]. The stakes are real: typical ERISA class settlements run $8-15M before fees, threatening fiduciary insurance [Multnomah Group, Inc. — _QhwEj0_Hrg @ 00:01:39].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not sign the annual gag-clause attestation, renew any vendor contract, or extend any broker or consultant agreement until gag clauses are confirmed removed, compensation disclosures in dollar figures are on file, PBM definitions are audited, and liability terms are locked into the RFP.

worksheets.title: Workers' Comp Mod Correction, Classification & Recovery Tracker
worksheets.purpose: Verify the experience mod and class codes that set workers' comp premium, control the claims and reserves that drive the mod, prepare for premium audits, and recover dollars lost to clawbacks and ERISA liens.
instructions: Obtain the current experience rating worksheet and the last five years of loss runs, and have the broker explain each line.
Compare every class code against the work employees actually perform, and keep time records for any split payroll.
Challenge open reserves before loss data is reported, since reserves weigh the same as paid dollars in the mod.
Assign one named owner for claims monitoring, light duty, and audit documentation, because what is not written down did not happen [RapidSync — pzqZsKtSynY @ 00:03:31].
Route every overpayment demand and lien through verification before any money moves, and never pay to make a demand disappear.

fields.name: emod_baseline
fields.prompt: Record your current experience mod, standard premium, the three policy years feeding the calculation, and the dollar premium difference between your mod and a 1.00 average, so the cost of every point above or below average is visible.
fields.example: On a $200k base premium, a 0.75 mod produces $150k while a 1.50 mod produces $300k; at a 10% margin, that extra $100k takes about $1M in additional sales to cover [Employers Group — XYYaHz216lk @ 00:17:14]. A couple of moderate claims can flip a 0.8 to a 1.2 for three years, so track it annually.

fields.name: minimum_mod_gap
fields.prompt: Calculate your minimum possible mod by dividing the stabilizing value by expected totals from the rating worksheet, then compare the premium at your current mod against the premium at that minimum to size the money you leave on the table.
fields.example: Take the stabilizing value over expected totals to get the minimum mod [Amaxx | Workers' Comp for Employers — z2GYx81GGEM @ 00:01:47]. A $500,000 manual premium company at a 0.8 credit mod pays $400,000 versus $200,000 at its 0.4 minimum, paying twice what it could with zero claim costs [Amaxx | Workers' Comp for Employers — z2GYx81GGEM @ 00:05:12].

fields.name: mod_worksheet_verification
fields.prompt: Walk through your experience rating worksheet line by line, checking payroll, class codes, primary and excess loss splits at your state's split point, and medical-only claim weighting, then list every discrepancy you will submit for correction before renewal.
fields.example: Some experts believe 60 to 70 percent of mods are wrong, and no bureau, carrier, or broker is responsible for verifying accuracy [The Coyle Group - Business Insurance — V5MJi6gMjSg @ 00:04:19]. Illinois uses a $30,000 split point, Indiana $18,500, Wisconsin $21,500 [JJ Doorhy & Associates — cgxTiDoClOs @ 00:14:35], and a $100 medical-only claim enters as $30.

fields.name: reserve_review
fields.prompt: List every open claim with its current reserve, the adjuster's rationale, and whether the reserve still matches the injury's actual trajectory, then record the date you challenged any inflated reserve before loss data was reported to the rating bureau.
fields.example: A $50,000 reserve on a claim impacts the mod the same as $50,000 paid out [JJ Doorhy & Associates — cgxTiDoClOs @ 00:12:03], so verify every open reserve before data goes to NCCI [JJ Doorhy & Associates — cgxTiDoClOs @ 00:12:21]. The most common mistake is no one monitoring claims experience [The Coyle Group - Business Insurance — Nfw1Tq_wDio @ 00:07:03].

fields.name: class_code_review
fields.prompt: List each governing class code, the payroll assigned to it, and the work actually performed by employees in that code, then identify any operation that may belong in a lower-rated classification and the time records supporting any payroll split.
fields.example: A mental-health program misclassified as home health care moved to a doctor's office code, cutting premium about 80% on $2.5M payroll with no new carrier and no negotiation [Insurance for Entrepreneurs — abb1Gjc-5z4 @ 00:03:59]. Without actual time records, the whole payroll goes to the highest-rated code at audit [Nia Brooks — POU9QtCmQZk @ 00:06:07].

fields.name: subcontractor_certificates
fields.prompt: Inventory every subcontractor used during the policy period, attach each certificate of insurance, and note whether it excludes owners, covers clerical work only, or lapsed mid-project, before the annual premium auditor reviews those same certificates.
fields.example: Run a class code review and check every subcontractor certificate for excluded owners and clerical-only coverage before the auditor does [WorkCompConsultants — tkOuTso-3RA @ 00:01:52]; [The Coyle Group - Business Insurance — 7sfUUlxeHHk @ 00:08:42]. Refusing the annual audit brings a charge up to 3x annual premium, collections, a worse e-mod, and possible cancellation [Insurance Brokers of Arizona — TZ9e1Sq1WJw @ 00:00:47].

fields.name: return_to_work_plan
fields.prompt: Describe your light-duty and return-to-work program, including who obtains doctor approval for modified duty, which on-site or nonprofit placements are available, and how lost-time days will be minimized so indemnity dollars stay off the loss runs.
fields.example: Once doctor-approved light duty is offered, the worker cannot refuse it; many dislike desk or nonprofit placements and heal faster, and some carriers partner with nonprofits so those indemnity dollars stay off loss runs and out of the mod [JJ Doorhy & Associates — cgxTiDoClOs @ 00:18:28]. Dedicated comp carriers with their own nurses push workers back sooner [ClinardInsGroup — -hUWvUBIr1A @ 00:02:10].

fields.name: small_claim_policy
fields.prompt: Write your rule for handling minor injuries, covering first aid versus recordable treatment, when if ever a small claim is paid outside the policy, and which risks such as overpayment, abusive claims, and Medicare penalties you weighed first.
fields.example: Have the clinic dispense 600 mg of ibuprofen instead of 800 mg, since the 800 mg dose turns a first aid into a recordable claim [Employers Group — XYYaHz216lk @ 00:45:27]. Before paying a small claim directly, weigh lost Texas Star Network savings, overpayment, abusive claims and Medicare penalties against the mod hit [Texas Mutual Insurance Co — gt3I3IxlEkE @ 00:02:34].

fields.name: overpayment_clawback
fields.prompt: For any bulk overpayment demand or retroactive denial, record the auditor's claimed authority, the look-back period cited, the timeline of notices, and the lien or administrative review request you filed to preserve rights instead of paying voluntarily.
fields.example: Never refund a bulk clawback voluntarily; the voluntary payment doctrine waives objections, and silence plus payment can equal acceptance [Medical Lien Management, Inc. — k60NAIUrnWA @ 00:08:19]. Verify the timeline, the auditor's authority, and the 12- or 24-month look-back first, then preserve rights through a lien or administrative review request [Medical Lien Management, Inc. — k60NAIUrnWA @ 00:12:56].

fields.name: erisa_lien_negotiation
fields.prompt: For each ERISA health plan lien asserted against an injury settlement, record the face amount, the date you sent a 1024(b)(4) document request to the plan administrator, itemization errors found, and the reduced amount negotiated before settlement.
fields.example: Send the 1024(b)(4) request to the plan administrator, never the vendor, and hold the $110-per-day penalty as leverage [synergy. — 6-UxSZMCtMg @ 00:21:17]. Audit itemizations for duplicates, unrelated claims, lump sums, and paid-over-billed lines [synergy. — 6-UxSZMCtMg @ 00:28:18]. Reported reductions run 30-78%, including $1.2M cut to $387k [synergy. — 6-UxSZMCtMg @ 00:39:22].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not accept a renewal quote, sign off on a premium audit, refund an overpayment demand, or settle a case carrying an ERISA lien until the mod worksheet is verified, reserves are challenged, class codes and subcontractor certificates are reviewed, and lien itemizations are audited.
